# Scenes

<a id="checkpoints"></a>

## Checkpoints

Topic `checkpoints`.

Fields: `checkpoints[].id`, `name`, `objective`, `type` (all required), `start`, `state_snapshot`, `player_name`, `player_text`, `target_turn_length` (`schema.ts` `Checkpoint`, `validate/checkpoints.ts` `readCheckpoint`).

- **What it does.** A beat. `type: "anchor"` beats are authored and guaranteed; `type: "intermediate"` beats are bridges and must lead on to an anchor. Exactly one beat has `start: true`. The `objective` is one sentence of what the beat is for; unless the beat has its own author's note, it is injected as an objective line. `state_snapshot` is what the story expects to be true while the beat is active (a generation target, not a write). `player_name` and `player_text` are what the player sees for the beat. `target_turn_length` is how many turns the beat should breathe; a stall re-read starts only after the larger of one and a half times that and six turns.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "ruined-gate", "name": "The Ruined Gate", "objective": "Agree terms with the guide and find a way through the gate.", "type": "anchor", "player_name": "The Gate in the Water", "tension_target": "calm", "target_turn_length": 5 }`.
- **Bad.** An objective that narrates the outcome; a `player_name` that tells the player what will happen there.
- **If wrong.** `player_name` shows to the player, so a name like "The Boatman's Betrayal" gives away what happens there. Keep player copy short (about 48 characters for a name and 200 for a text), true on every path in, and free of macros and spoilers. An intermediate with no anchor beyond it is a load error; a generated stub with no anchor beyond it is `stub-no-anchor`.

<a id="objective-agency"></a>

## Objectives and player agency

Topic `objective-agency`.

Fields: `checkpoints[].agency` (`protect_player_choice`, `never_narrate_player_action`, `objective_kind`, `alternate`, `player_attempts_only`, `skip`) and the story's `objective_block` (`schema.ts` `AgencyPolicy`, `engine/agency.ts`, `validate/checkpoints.ts` `readAgency`).

- **What it does.** The defaults are the policy, even when `agency` is absent (`DEFAULT_AGENCY`): narration never writes the player accepting what they refused or going where they declined, never writes the player's own words and decisions, never decides how the player feels, what they believe or what they conclude (characters and the inner voice may guess at it, never settle it), and the objective is world pressure. `objective_kind: "world_pressure"` lets the world press, answer and escalate without the player's compliance. `objective_kind: "player_action"` makes the world present the situation and the choice, then stop. `alternate` names a beat to recover to when the player refuses the prepared route. `player_attempts_only` makes the world decide whether the player's stated attempt works. `skip: false` takes **Skip ahead** (the story card, `/story skip`) away at this beat; absent, the player may skip ahead wherever the install switch `talk.skipAhead` is on (off until its blind rating passes). A skip is one reply from the story's narrator (the `view: "omniscient"` member), else the beat's `talk_control.lead`: it tells the time passing up to the next part of the day at most (the story read then moves the clock one part, as for any reply), and stops early when an echo, rumor, commitment, quest or agenda step falls due. `objective_block: "off"` stops the objective line being injected story-wide.
- **Good.** `"agency": { "objective_kind": "player_action", "player_attempts_only": true, "alternate": "the-keepers-camp" }` at a beat where the player must choose a side. The `alternate` is an intermediate that rejoins the story.
- **Bad.** `alternate` naming the beat itself; `player_action` on a beat that should advance whether or not the player engages; `skip: false` everywhere, which leaves travel and waiting to be played out turn by turn.
- **If wrong.** An unknown `alternate` leaves a refusal nowhere to go (`agency-alternate-unknown`); one naming the beat sends the player back into it (`agency-alternate-is-self`). A story with no `alternate` anywhere is a rail. Guidance that scripts a schedule ("the keepers lead the party…") produces a time skip the player never chose.

<a id="open-stretches"></a>

## Open stretches

Topic `open-stretches`.

Fields: `checkpoints[].stretch` (`mode`, `pace`, `pull_after`, `max_turns`, `offer`, `arrive_when`) and the code quality `player_turns_in_checkpoint` (`schema.ts` `CheckpointStretch`, `engine/stretch.ts`, `validate/stretch.ts`, `pacing/quiet.ts`, `generation/encounters.ts`).

- **What it does.** `stretch: { "mode": "open" }` on an intermediate makes it free play between two fixed points: no objective line is injected there (the story's `objective_block` still governs every other beat), it is never expanded into a beat chain, and a long quiet run is neither a stall re-read nor a refusal. The narrator is told to follow what the player starts. `pace` (`brief`, `unhurried`, `long`) sets `pull_after` to 3, 6 or 10 **player turns** (a group round of several replies to one player line is one turn; an out-of-character line is none); an explicit `pull_after` wins. Past it the world pulls gently toward the next place with hooks (gentle, then steady three turns later); the narrator is told the place by name, the public name (or name) of the beat the arrival exit leads to. `max_turns` only makes the pull plain, and never moves the party or narrates the move. The `objective` stays for the readers (the arrival read needs it), but the narrator never gets it as a task: no objective line, and `{{story_current_checkpoint}}` and the inner voice name the scene only. The player leaves by their own move: `arrive_when` is the arrival gate, and it must be the gate of every one of the stretch's exits: a second exit on another gate (a turn count, a constant) is refused. Declare `player_turns_in_checkpoint` as an `int` with `source: "code"` to read the count in gates or macros. In the Studio, the Checkpoints tab's **Open stretch** panel (intermediates) sets the pace, the pull, the plain pull, the encounter offer and the arrival exit, and names any exit that would be refused; the wizard sets it with `updateCheckpoint` and `patch.stretch` (`null` clears it).
- **Encounters.** `"offer": ["encounters"]` asks the story to prepare a small menu: while the player is one beat before the stretch, or in it, a background pass writes 3 to 5 optional situations (a title and one or two sentences each) through the same authoring route, the same critic and the same agency policy as a generated chain. A situation has no outcome, no gate, no progress, no objective and no exit, and none is needed for anything; one the player ignores is simply gone. The code checks refuse a pool outside 3 to 5, a repeated title, a long title, a situation that writes the player's own act, and any outcome-shaped key; a pool the critic fails waits in This chat → Author's Scheduler tab (Regenerate) and is never used. The narrator sees the menu only when the stretch is **quiet**: at least `pull_after` player turns have passed and no quality named by any of the stretch's exit gates (`arrive_when` included, counters such as `player_turns_in_checkpoint` left out) has changed value over the last 3 player turns, read from the boundary snapshots. It is told to offer at most one, never to resolve it for the player and never to name a title. Pool titles and situations are author-only: no player surface shows them.
- **Open opening on an anchor.** `stretch: { "mode": "open", "pace": "brief" }` on an **anchor** keeps the objective line, `{{story_current_checkpoint}}` task text and the inner voice's task out for the anchor's first `pull_after` player turns (at most 10), then the anchor reads as any other. An opening has no `arrive_when`, `max_turns` or `offer`: the anchor's own exits work as usual and nothing moves the party. The anchor keeps its ordinary `player_text`: the player surfaces that show it (the Where-you-are note, the main-line widget, the player projection that Ask and suggestions read, the entry note) hold it back while the opening lasts and show it from the first player turn after the opening, like the objective line. The Studio's **Open opening** panel (anchors) sets it.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "on-the-road", "name": "On the road", "objective": "", "type": "intermediate", "stretch": { "mode": "open", "pace": "unhurried", "offer": ["encounters"], "arrive_when": { "q": "reached_gate", "op": "==", "v": true } } }` with the exit `on-the-road → ruined-gate` gated on the same `reached_gate == true`; and `{ "id": "harbour", "type": "anchor", "stretch": { "mode": "open", "pace": "brief" } }` for a scene that should breathe for three turns before it asks anything.
- **Bad.** An open stretch whose exit waits on `progress_toward_<anchor>` or carries a progress effect (refused: a filled counter ending a scene is the corridor this mode removes); `player_text` on an open stretch (refused: the player sees the scene name, never a task); an opening past 10 turns. An anchor's `player_text` is fine: it is hidden during the opening and shown after.
- **If wrong.** `pressure` and `trigger` are refused as not built yet: complications are not built yet; the quiet state only gates the encounter menu today. An `arrive_when` that matches no exit is a load error, so the stretch cannot trap the player. A pool whose generation failed is retried once on arrival and then waits for the author; with no usable pool the stretch plays as a plain open stretch.

<a id="tension"></a>

## Tension targets

Topic `tension`.

Field: `checkpoints[].tension_target` (`calm`, `stirring`, `tense`, `critical`, `peak`).

- **What it does.** The tension the beat aims for. Tension is read as one of the five levels each turn, smoothed, and compared with the target and the dramatic shape; the narrator gets a one-line steer.
- **Good.** `calm` at the gate, `stirring` when the party enters the flooded hall, `critical` in the ambush, `peak` at the finale.
- **Bad.** Every beat at `peak`; a target at odds with the beat's objective (a quiet negotiation at `critical`).
- **If wrong.** Pacing pushes the narrator the wrong way. The measured scale also overshoots on calm play (a calm scene can read as climbing toward "critical"), so do not rely on a gate over `tension_current` for a quiet beat.

<a id="opening-scene"></a>

## The opening scene

Topic `opening-scene`.

Fields: each card's `first_mes` (on the SillyTavern card), the start checkpoint's `cast_changes`, a scripted `onEnter` npc reply with `new_chat_only`, and an opening hook: an `llm` `onEnter` npc reply with `new_chat_only` (`validate/checkpoints.ts` `readCheckpointEffects`; `runtime/effectsApplier.ts` `openingHook`; rule text `FIRST_MESSAGE_RULE`, `OPENING_CAST_RULE` in `src/copilot/prompts.ts`).

- **What it does.** In a group every card with a first message greets at once when the chat opens. A scripted `onEnter` reply with `new_chat_only: true` posts only into an empty chat, so it is the story's own opener. An `llm` `onEnter` reply with `new_chat_only: true` is the **opening hook**: a party member's own line right after the opening, before the player's first message. Order on a fresh chat: every scripted opener in declaration order (the chat is checked for emptiness once, before the first), then the start beat's staging (world info, author note, cast), then the start beat's other entering lines in declaration order, then the hook. Nothing posts until the identity step is settled, so an entering line never lands before the opener. The story's own opener never holds back its own beat: even when it ends on a question to the player, the entering lines and the hook still post. The hook posts once per chat, only into a chat whose opening just ran with no player line yet, and only while its member is switched on in the group (it waits for the start beat's `cast_changes` to land). Give it `ask_player: true` to have the member turn to the player and ask one thing in their own voice, and an `instruction` for what to bring up; both reach that member, privately, for that one reply only. `after_member` (for example the narrator) holds it unless the line before it is that member's. It is a forced reply, so no speaker chain follows it: the player answers next.
- **Good.** One narrator card with an empty first message; the start beat disables the later cast; one `new_chat_only` opener, then one hook: `{ "trigger": "onEnter", "member": "Ruins Narrator", "kind": "scripted", "new_chat_only": true, "text": "You came to Lowmarsh because the water is low at last…" }`, `{ "trigger": "onEnter", "member": "Mara", "kind": "llm", "new_chat_only": true, "ask_player": true, "after_member": "Ruins Narrator", "instruction": "Mara has been watching the road; she wants to know if the newcomer saw the riders." }`.
- **Bad.** First messages written for each character's later beat. A greeting that addresses the player as a role ("You are the lamplighter") while a card plays that role. A hook whose instruction asks what the player does ("ask what they will do next") or says what the player feels.
- **If wrong.** Every member greets at once in a fresh group, and a character meant to arrive later can give away a twist at message 0. `new_chat_only` is accepted only on an `onEnter` reply. A start beat with an opener and no hook gets the info diagnostic `opening-narrator-only`: "Only the narrator speaks before the player's first message, so nobody in the party turns to the player at the start." A hook whose member is switched off when it would post is skipped (the journal says so). Swiping the hook (or any line written under an instruction) regenerates it with the same one-shot direction; deleting the hook does not post it again.
